description: Beacon Audit: briefing, radio calls and outcome text.

briefing: Three nav beacons in {system} have missed their audit. Fly close to each and hold until it reports. Mind the pirates that have been seen nearby.
Routine audit of the beacon chain at {station}. Slow down, close to 400 metres, hold. The beacon will not answer a ship that is moving.
success: All three beacons report and the raiders are gone. {client} files the audit as complete.
failure: The audit is incomplete. {client} will send someone else, with a note on your file.
The beacons are still unlogged. The order stands.
radio-beacons: Wren: Beacons on the board, three of them. Section four says we hold at four hundred metres. I would like to hold at four hundred metres.
Wren: First beacon ahead. Matching speed. Please do the same, Captain.
radio-wing: Wren here, on your wing. Flight Officer Wren, in case Command did not say.
Wren: Wing in position. I have the manual open on my second screen.
radio-raiders: Wren: Contact, three, behind us. They are not on the audit schedule.
Wren: Pirates. Captain, may I say weapons free?
Wren: Three fighters from astern. I believe they are the sort we are meant to report.

description: Customs Run: briefing, radio calls and outcome text.

briefing: A freighter is running from {station} without a clearance. The Concord would like it stopped. It has two escorts and will not stop for a polite request.
Customs flagged a hull leaving {system} with a forged manifest. Intercept the {runner}. Force is authorised, which is a phrase I have never enjoyed writing.
success: The {runner} is stopped and its manifest, such as it was, recovered. {client} pays.
Smuggler down, cargo seized, paperwork started. {client} pays {captain}.
failure: The {runner} is through the gate. {client} writes a short, unkind memo.
The runner escaped. Customs is unamused.
radio-runner: Wren: There she is. Freighter {runner}. I have her manifest and it is fiction.
Wren: Target at range. Under section nine we may demand she heave to. She will not.
radio-guard: Wren: Two escorts, loose formation. Do they know we have seen them?
Wren: Fighter escorts. Nothing we cannot manage.
radio-late: Wren: Two more from starboard. I suspect they were paid to be late.
Wren: Reinforcements, right. Captain, please do not let the paperwork pile up.

description: Dry Tanks: briefing, radio calls and outcome text.

briefing: The freighter {stranded} has drifted dead in {system} with dry tanks. We are the nearest. Match speed, hold close and the transfer will take half a minute. Pirates have heard the distress call.
A stranded hauler needs fuel. Fly alongside the {stranded}, hold still relative to her, and keep the pirates off while you do. They are already on their way.
success: The {stranded} has fuel and a heading. {client} pays and the master sends a case of something undrinkable.
Transfer complete, pirates dead. {client} pays {captain}. The master of the {stranded} sends thanks and a very long invoice of his own.
failure: The {stranded} is lost. {client} pays nothing and starts an inquiry.
No fuel delivered. The {stranded} is still drifting, or is wreckage.
radio-stranded: {stranded}: Concord patrol, thank God. We are bone dry. Please come alongside and do not hurry. Actually, please hurry.
{stranded}: Our reactor is cold and the master is praying. Match speed and we will take what you can spare.
radio-first: Wren: Two contacts closing. Captain, we cannot transfer fuel and dodge at once. Perhaps one at a time.
Wren: Pirates. They did hear the call.
radio-second: Wren: Three fighters and a gunship, right. The gunship wants the freighter. Please do not let it have her.
Wren: More. The gunship is going for the {stranded}.
radio-third: Wren: Frigate behind us with an escort. I did not read about this in the manual.
Wren: Last of them, I hope. A frigate and three fighters, astern.

description: Envoy's Passage: briefing, radio calls and outcome text.

briefing: A Concord envoy is crossing {system} to meet a Khanate delegation. You are the escort, with two of our own. The Khanates have promised an honour guard. Take that promise at its face value, but keep your safeties off.
Escort the envoy {envoy} through {system}. The delegation is meant to meet us halfway and show us courtesy. The Commodore says to expect courtesy. The Commodore also says to expect otherwise.
success: The {envoy} is clear and the envoy is shaken but unharmed. {client} files a protest in three copies.
Envoy delivered, honour guard dispersed with prejudice. {client} pays {captain}.
failure: The {envoy} is lost. {client} suspends talks and starts drafting the speech.
The envoy is dead. This will be remembered.
radio-envoy: {envoy}: Concord escort, this is the envoy. Please keep the ride smooth. I have a speech to give.
Wren: Envoy in the middle, two of ours on her flanks. We stay close.
radio-greeters: Wren: The honour guard has arrived. A frigate, the {greeter}, and four fighters. They are not hailing.
Wren: Khanate ships ahead. Weapons are hot. Captain, I think they have read the protocol differently.
radio-knives: Wren: Gunships behind us, going for the envoy. That is a clear breach.
Wren: Two bombers from astern and fighters. They were never an honour guard.

description: Quiet Listening: briefing, radio calls and outcome text.

briefing: Two Khanate pickets are sitting in {system}, apparently doing nothing. Command wants a scan of both. Go close, hold, and do not shoot first. A ship you destroy is a ship you cannot scan.
Reconnaissance. The {enemy} have parked a picket line in {system} and said nothing about it. Scan each ship, then the tenders if you can. Expect a reaction.
success: The scans are clean. The tenders carry torpedo stock and boarding gear, a great deal of it. {client} pays {captain} and goes quiet.
Data in hand. The picket is not a picket. {client} pays and calls a meeting.
failure: No scan, or too late for it to matter. {client} asks you to try again with fewer guns firing.
The scan failed. Command is blind.
radio-pickets: Wren: Two frigates holding, no lights, no greetings. I have them at three thousand five hundred metres.
Wren: Pickets ahead. They are sitting still, which is what worries me.
radio-screen: Wren: Fighters circling the pickets. Low and slow. They have not seen us yet. Please do not startle them.
Wren: Screen of four. If we scan from within seven hundred metres they will notice.
radio-tenders: Wren: Tenders on the right, three of them, heavy and low. That is a lot of stores for a picket.
Wren: Supply hulls, holding. Captain, these are the interesting ones.
radio-react: Wren: Interceptors behind us. They noticed the scan.
Wren: Four hunters, astern. We have what we need. Let us go.
radio-wake: Wren: Jump flash. Cruiser and fighters, far side. We have been rather expensive for them.
Wren: Heavy reinforcement arriving. Time to leave, Captain.

description: Cut the Tithe Fleet: briefing, radio calls and outcome text.

briefing: A Khanate convoy is carrying ore and guns to a staging point near {system}. Cut it. The {enemy} screen it well and you will not be the only fast ship out there.
Intercept. Four freighters, an escort frigate and a fighter screen. The Commodore has authorised a bonus for the freighters. I am asked to say that it is for the freighters, and not for the ace.
success: The tithe fleet is burning. {client} pays {captain} and files it under deterrence.
Convoy destroyed. The {enemy} will have to find their guns elsewhere. {client} pays.
failure: The convoy gets through. {client} pays nothing, and Quill wants the unspent ammunition back.
The freighters escape. The staging point will be ready.
radio-convoy: Wren: Convoy ahead, four freighters, one frigate, the {warden}. They are riding low.
Wren: There they are. Fat, slow and well guarded.
radio-screen: Wren: Six fighters on the screen. We should take them before the freighters can bolt.
Wren: Screen is up. They have seen us. Weapons free.
radio-ace: Skarn Redtooth: Concord. Little ships, little lawyers. I will take your wing as a trophy.
Wren: That is the Redtooth. Captain, they say he has forty kills. I would prefer he did not have forty-one.
radio-hounds: Wren: Gunships and fighters from the left. The Khanates call it a hunt.
Wren: More of them, left side. Keep the freighters in sight.

description: The Clause Holds: briefing, radio calls and outcome text.

briefing: The {enemy} are coming for the {flagship} with everything they have. The Commodore will hold {system}. We have eight minutes until relief. Protect the {flagship} and keep the fighters between her and the bombers.
The {flagship} will not move and will not be moved. Relief is on its way and will arrive late, which is how the Concord does everything. Hold.
success: Relief arrives to find the {flagship} scorched and standing. {client} pays {captain} the full fee. The Commodore calls it a satisfactory outcome. Quill calls it an expensive one.
The line held. {client} pays and awards you a medal, with the paperwork to follow.
failure: The {flagship} is lost. {client} pays nothing and begins the inquiry.
{system} is lost and the {flagship} with it. This will take a long time to put right.
radio-line: Marsh: All hands, this is the Commodore. We have eight minutes. I want every fighter in the air and every gun on the bombers.
Marsh: Concord ships, hold. The {flagship} holds. That is an order and a request.
radio-first: Wren: Eight fighters and four gunships. The gunships want the {flagship}. They will not have her.
Wren: First wave, ahead. Stay close to the {flagship}.
radio-siege: Wren: Two cruisers on the left with heavy guns. We cannot let them settle.
Wren: Siege cruisers. They will batter the {flagship} if left alone.
radio-carrier: Wren: A carrier, overhead. The {target}. Her wing is already out.
Wren: Jump flash. {target}, carrier class, and eight interceptors.
radio-ace: Skarn Redtooth: Lawyer. I came for your Commodore. Fly, or be flown past.
Wren: The Redtooth is back and behind us. Captain, he is yours.
radio-relief: Marsh: Relief is here. Well held, all of you.
Wren: Friendly fleet inbound. I never thought I would be so glad to see an administrative column.
